metas.name: Master and Commander: The Far Side of the World
metas.description:
Captures a ship as a complete working system. During the Napoleonic Wars a British frigate hunts a French ship around South America — seamanship, weather and hierarchy, and a captain whose naturalist friend would rather be cataloguing species in the Galápagos.

During the Napoleonic Wars, a brash British captain pushes his ship and crew to their limits in pursuit of a formidable French war vessel around South America.

metas.name: The Battle of Algiers
metas.description:
Captures insurgency and counter-insurgency as procedures. Staged like newsreel, with no hero on either side, as Algiers becomes a chessboard of cells, checkpoints and bombs.

In the 1950s, fear and violence escalate as the people of Algiers fight for independence from the French government.

metas.name: Come and See
metas.description:
Captures war as it is done to a child. Belarus, 1943: a boy joins the partisans beaming and ages a lifetime in days; it is not the gore, it is his face.

After finding a rifle, a Belarusian teenager joins Soviet partisans in World War II and is swept into the harrowing realities of Nazi occupation.

metas.name: Grave of the Fireflies
metas.description:
Captures war as two children slowly running out of everything. A brother tries to keep his little sister fed and cheerful in Kobe, 1945, making worse decisions out of pride.

A young boy and his little sister struggle to survive in Japan during World War II.

metas.name: Waltz with Bashir
metas.description:
Captures a soldier's memory with a hole in it. Animated interviews as the director tries to recover what he did in Beirut in 1982, ending with footage that breaks the animation open.

An Israeli film director interviews fellow veterans of the 1982 invasion of Lebanon to reconstruct his own memories of his term of service in that conflict.

metas.name: Dr. Strangelove
metas.description:
Captures nuclear annihilation as a bureaucratic procedure. Generals, presidents and advisors in rooms — vain, procedural and insane — while the world ends by checklist.

After a rogue U.S. general orders an unauthorized nuclear attack on the Soviet Union, leaders in the War Room race to prevent global catastrophe.

metas.name: Barry Lyndon
metas.description:
Captures a rise and fall narrated like fate already happened. An Irish opportunist climbs 18th-century society through duels, war and marriage, shot like paintings, with a narrator who keeps telling you the ending early.

An Irish rogue wins the heart of a rich widow and assumes her dead husband's aristocratic position in 18th-century England.

metas.name: Lawrence of Arabia
metas.description:
Captures a man inventing himself at desert scale. Nearly four hours: the landscape is a character, and so is the gap between the legend being built and the person inside it.

The story of T.E. Lawrence, the English officer who successfully united and led the diverse, often warring, Arab tribes during World War I in order to fight the Turks.

metas.name: Army of Shadows
metas.description:
Captures resistance as cold, lonely procedure. French Resistance, 1942: safe houses, coded phrases, informers executed badly — no glamour and almost no hope, filmed like a heist movie in mourning.

An account of underground resistance fighters in Nazi-occupied France.

metas.name: Paths of Glory
metas.description:
Captures military honour used to cover a command failure. After a suicidal attack fails, three soldiers are chosen to be executed for cowardice to make the point, and their colonel tries law against arithmetic.

A colonel defends three of his soldiers in a court-martial after they abandon a suicidal attack.

metas.name: Pan's Labyrinth
metas.description:
Captures a child's fantasy as the only available resistance. Spain, 1944: a girl with a fascist stepfather descends to a faun's tasks while the adult war continues above ground, and fantasy is never 'just' escape.

In 1944 Francoist Spain, an imaginative young girl meets a faun who tells her she's a princess and that she must prove her worthiness by completing three dangerous tasks.

metas.name: Incendies
metas.description:
Captures two children learning their mother's life was a war they knew nothing about. Montreal twins, a will, two sealed letters, and a journey into a fictionalised Lebanon their mother never described — it hits like a Greek tragedy.

Twins journey to the Middle East to discover their family history and fulfill their mother's last wishes.

metas.name: Lust, Caution
metas.description:
Captures an espionage performance becoming the real feeling it was faking. In occupied Shanghai, a student actress is assigned to seduce a collaborationist official so he can be killed, over years of mahjong games and assignations.

During World War II era, a young woman, Wang Jiazhi, gets swept up in a dangerous game of emotional intrigue with a powerful political figure, Mr. Yee.

metas.name: The Shop on Main Street
metas.description:
Captures collaboration at its smallest and most cowardly. A Slovak carpenter handed a Jewish widow's button shop under Aryanization laws hides her instead of profiting — comic and gentle, until the roundup comes anyway.

A carpenter in the Fascist Slovak State is appointed "Aryan controller" of a Jewish widow's store.

metas.name: Quo Vadis, Aida?
metas.description:
Captures catastrophe processed as procedure. Srebrenica, 1995, through a UN translator moving names between lists, gates and buses — horror administered in queues and stamps, with everyone following protocol.

Aida is a translator for the UN in the small town of Srebrenica. When the Serbian army takes over the town, her family is among the thousands of citizens looking for shelter in the UN camp.

metas.name: The Zone of Interest
metas.description:
Captures evil as a domestic soundscape. The Höss family gardens, swims and hosts lunches on the other side of the Auschwitz wall; you see almost nothing of the camp and hear it in every scene.

The commandant of Auschwitz and his wife strive to build a dream life for their family in a house next to the camp.

metas.name: Hearts and Minds
metas.description:
Captures how a country talks itself into a war and then can't talk itself out of the damage. Vietnam told by everyone it passed through — generals, pilots, Vietnamese villagers, American POWs and grieving parents.

A startling and courageous landmark documentary that unflinchingly confronted the United States' involvement in Vietnam at the height of the controversy that surrounded it.

metas.name: Shoah
metas.description:
Captures memory itself as evidence. Nine and a half hours with not one frame of archival footage — only survivors, bystanders and perpetrators talking in the present tense, in the places where it happened. The most demanding film in the collection.

Claude Lanzmann's epic documentary recounts the story of the Holocaust through interviews with witnesses - perpetrators as well as survivors.

metas.name: For Sama
metas.description:
Captures war from inside a family instead of inside a news report. Waad Al-Kateab films five years of the siege of Aleppo as a letter to her baby daughter, explaining why they stayed.

An intimate and epic journey into a young woman's experience of war during the revolution in Aleppo, Syria.

metas.name: 20 Days in Mariupol
metas.description:
Captures the 2022 siege of Mariupol as the people inside it actually experienced its first twenty days. AP journalists trapped in the city keep filming because getting the footage out is the only thing that makes staying mean anything.

An AP team of Ukrainian journalists trapped in the besieged city of Mariupol struggle to continue their work documenting atrocities of the Russian invasion.

metas.name: S-21: The Khmer Rouge Killing Machine
metas.description:
Captures atrocity recalled as office procedure: survivor Vann Nath brings former Tuol Sleng guards back into the prison, where they re-enact their daily routines of shackling and paperwork and find nothing dramatic in their own memories.

A unique documentary on the notorious S-21 prison, today the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, with testimony by the only surviving prisoners and former Khmer Rouge guards.

metas.name: They Shall Not Grow Old
metas.description:
Captures the trenches suddenly populated by recognisable young men instead of ghosts. Peter Jackson restores jerky silent WWI footage to correct speed, colourises it, and adds voices reconstructed from veterans' interviews and lip-reading.

A documentary about World War I with never-before-seen footage to commemorate the centennial of the end of the war.

metas.name: The White Bird Marked with Black
metas.description:
Captures folk culture being torn by history. In the same Hutsul Carpathians as Shadows, four brothers in a village band end up on opposite sides of every border the war years drag across their valley, in images just as saturated.

A family struggles to survive in an area that was claimed as part of Rumania, Poland and Ukraine, all within a short span of time. When World War II comes, various family members choose different masters; some even choose to work for the Soviets. War, struggle, marriages, births, deaths--all these events punctuate the story of this large family.

metas.name: The Round-Up
metas.description:
Captures power as folk dance. On an endless white plain, authorities process prisoners from a peasant uprising through rituals of selection and betrayal, in Jancsó's choreographed long takes — nobody's psychology is explained, and the rituals are the point.

In Hungary, the national movement led by Kossuth has been crushed and the Austrian hegemony re-established, but partisans carry on with violent actions. In order to root out the guerilla, the army rounds up suspects and jails them...
